title: Introduce residency-proof cache and RBAC assertion serializer
author: Ava Kapoor
description:
Summary: Add a residency-proof caching layer to reduce per-request KMS provenance checks and introduce a compact RBAC assertion serializer for transit in headers and audit log entries. Motivation: KMS provenance checks and per-request RBAC evaluation were identified as a source of latency and increased KMS bills for chat/embedding hot paths (see ENG-4123). This PR implements a TTL-backed cache for residency proofs (signed KMS assertions) and a space-efficient, versioned serializer for RBAC v2 decision bundles so we can safely carry decision artifacts across services and persist them in audit records without blowing up storage or exposing sensitive raw blobs.

Design: The residency-proof cache is a small in-memory LRU + optional Redis backing; proofs are keyed by (tenant_id, geozone, proof-version) and validated against a minimal verifier on fetch. Cache entries respect proof expiry and a configurable soft-stale window for background refresh. The RBAC assertion serializer encodes assertion bundles (roles, grants, evaluation-timestamp, evaluation-hash) into a compressed, signed payload (v1) using protobuf + snappy and a compact header prefix for quick routing. Both components include feature flags and runtime knobs so rollout can be staged per-operator and per-region.

Checklist: 
- [x] Residency cache implementation and unit tests
- [x] Serializer implementation and unit tests
- [x] Integration tests (simulated KMS failures + cache fallback)
- [x] Docs: developer and ops guidance
- [x] Feature flags for staged rollout
- [x] Benchmarks: end-to-end p50 token latency reduced by ~12% in internal bench (small model, short seq)

Rollback plan: Feature flags can disable cache and serializer independently; disable serializer to revert to existing plain JSON RBAC envelope (no data migration needed). If cache causes correctness issues, we expire entries instantly and fall back to direct KMS verification.

Testing: Added unit tests for cache expiry, reconciliation, and race conditions; integration test harness simulates intermittent KMS latency and verifies fallbacks. Load bench scripts included under tools/bench/residency.

Related work: This complements ENG-4058 (batching + KV-cache improvements) and reduces the operational KMS traffic surface called out in SEC-88. See docs/security/residency-proofing.md for operator runbook.

Notes: CI initially failed on lint (gofmt) and a flaky integration test; both addressed in followups. This PR intentionally keeps the serialized assertion "v1" as opt-in to allow backward compatibility with older services.

release_notes: Add residency-proof cache (in-memory + optional Redis) to reduce KMS lookups and an opt-in compact RBAC assertion serializer (v1) to shrink audit payloads and improve cross-service transit efficiency. Rollout controlled via feature flags; see docs/security/residency-proofing.md for operator guidance.
notes_for_ops: Feature flags: residency.cache.enabled, residency.cache.redis_url, rbac.serializer.v1.enabled. Default: both disabled. Start with residency.cache.enabled=true for <5% of tenants and monitor residency_cache.stale_hits, cache_hit_ratio, and kms_outbound_rate. Serializer can be enabled regionally once all consumers understand v1 header or fallback is configured.
impact_summary: Expected reduction in KMS traffic (observed ~28% lower verifications in bench), p50 latency improvements on hot paths (~12%). Adds modest memory usage per service (configurable LRU size). No DB migrations. Backward compatible when serializer disabled.
